COMPREHENSIVE ONCOLOGY GENOMIC PROFILING REPORT

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sex: Male
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Institution: [redacted location]

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Prostate tissue
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Pathologic Diagnosis: Mixed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma
Tumor Content: ~40%

TEST PERFORMED
Comprehensive Oncology NGS Panel
- DNA Analysis: Hybrid capture-based target enrichment with parallel sequencing
- RNA Analysis: Fusion panel (attempted)

METHODOLOGY
DNA Extraction: Automated extraction kit from FFPE tissue
Library Preparation: Hybrid capture-based target enrichment
Sequencing Platform: Next-generation sequencing
Bioinformatics Pipeline: Variant calling for SNVs, indels, CNVs
Minimum Coverage Target: 500x

RESULTS SUMMARY

ACTIONABLE FINDINGS
1. BRCA2 c.9196C>T p.(Gln3066*) - Pathogenic variant detected
   - Variant Allele Frequency: 67%
   - Location: Exon 24
   - Clinical Significance: FDA-approved therapies available (PARP inhibitors)

DNA SEQUENCING RESULTS

Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic Variants:
Gene	Variant	VAF	Exon	Protein Change	Classification
BRCA2	c.9196C>T	67%	24	p.(Gln3066*)	Pathogenic

Quality Metrics:
- Mean Target Coverage: Below optimal
- Genes with Reduced Coverage (<100x): BRCA1, ATM, CDK12
- Overall Panel Performance: Suboptimal

RNA FUSION ANALYSIS
Result: Failed - Insufficient RNA quality

VARIANT DETAILS

BRCA2 c.9196C>T p.(Gln3066*)
- Transcript: NM_000059.3
- Consequence: Nonsense mutation resulting in premature stop codon
- Population Frequency: <0.001% (gnomAD)
- ClinVar Classification: Pathogenic
- ACMG Classification: Pathogenic (PVS1, PM2, PP5)
- Functional Impact: Loss of function due to protein truncation

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION

The detected BRCA2 pathogenic variant (c.9196C>T) results in a premature stop codon and is associated with homologous recombination deficiency. This finding has therapeutic implications for prostate cancer management:

1. PARP Inhibitor Sensitivity: Tumors with BRCA2 mutations demonstrate enhanced sensitivity to PARP inhibitors (e.g., olaparib, rucaparib)
2. Platinum Sensitivity: May indicate increased responsiveness to platinum-based chemotherapy
3. Germline Implications: The high variant allele frequency (67%) suggests this may be a germline variant

LIMITATIONS
1. Suboptimal sequencing coverage was observed across multiple genes including BRCA1, ATM, and CDK12, which may result in false-negative findings
2. RNA fusion analysis failed due to insufficient RNA quality
3. The mixed histology and moderate tumor content (40%) may affect variant detection sensitivity
4. This assay does not distinguish between somatic and germline variants

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Repeat testing on a separate tissue block is strongly recommended to confirm the BRCA2 variant before initiating targeted therapy
2. Genetic counseling and germline testing are advised given the high VAF and clinical implications for family members
3. Consider alternative specimen with higher tumor content if repeat testing is pursued
4. Clinical correlation with patient history and other diagnostic findings is recommended

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location]. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Medical Director
Date: [redacted date]
